shots.text: He ran from us. For the first time in two thousand years, the High King ran, and the gates of his city closed behind him.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Vael-Orrun, broken and smoking, fleeing up the road into the citadel; the gates booming shut.

shots.text: Gates are my trade. Let me.
shots.speaker: brannoc
shots.art_note: Brannoc stepping out in front of the army with his hammer on his shoulder, the forge-light in his arm glowing.

shots.text: Our towers held the camp. Everything else we had went up the roads: every soldier, every hero, every one of them.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The army pouring up the three roads toward the gates: red-plate footmen, pikes, hounds, hawk-riders overhead, the ram rolling under its hides.

shots.text: At the inner gate, the Dawnblade turned and held it open for all of us. She held it until the last of us were through.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Seraphel in the inner gate, armour drained of colour, sword blazing, holding the doors apart as the army runs past her. Her light goes out.

shots.text: Tell Ysolde I saw one more dawn. That was all I wanted.
shots.speaker: seraphel
